data.description:
## Context / Problem
Store-wide maintenance walks visit every ticket directory on every run: the fsck scan loops (`_ticket_dirs` iterations in src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py) and the compact-all sweep (src/rebar/_commands/compact.py::compact_all_cli) are O(all tickets ever created). As the store grows, archived tickets — cold, already folded to a SNAPSHOT, excluded from default `list` — dominate that walk and make routine health checks and sweeps slower for no operational value. `ticket list` already has the pattern to copy: default excludes archived (marker fast-path at reducer/_api.py with compiled-state confirmation) with an explicit `--include-archived` override.

## Approach
Introduce one shared helper (in the module fsck_scan already imports `_ticket_dirs` from) that yields ACTIVE ticket dirs by default — skipping dirs whose net archival state is archived, using the `.archived` marker as the fast-path and the existing `_is_net_archived`-style event-name confirmation, the exact semantics `list` uses — with an `include_archived` flag to yield everything. Switch the fsck scan loops and the compact-all sweep to it; add `--include-archived` to `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` (and thread it through their JSON/usage lines). Default = active-only for both: an archived ticket was already folded and health-checked on its way out, and any deep audit reaches it with the flag. To keep the archive path itself sound, `rebar archive` continues to work as today; a final fold for a just-archived ticket still happens via the scheduled sweep run with `--include-archived` (documented), so no events are ever stranded unfolded. Positive rationale: this reuses the archive marker + net-archival semantics that default `list` has proven, rather than inventing a second notion of active.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py — scan loops take the active-only iterator; `--include-archived` flag threading.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — CLI flag + usage + JSON passthrough.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — compact_all_cli default active-only + `--include-archived`.
- tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py (new) — visited-set coverage both ways.
- docs/user-guide.md — document the default and the override.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture store with N archived (marker + ARCHIVED event) and M active tickets; default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all --dry-run` visit exactly the M active dirs (assert on the visited set / reported counts); with `--include-archived` they visit N+M.
- Edge: a ticket dir with a stale marker but NO net-archived state (reverted archive) is still visited by default (the confirmation step, not the marker alone, decides); an archived ticket with a corrupt event file IS reported when `--include-archived` is passed (deep audit still works).
- Empty store: both commands succeed with zero visits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` visit only non-archived tickets, and `--include-archived` restores the full walk; checked by the visited-set test.
- [ ] A reverted-archive ticket (stale marker) is never skipped by default; checked by the edge test.
- [ ] Usage lines and docs/user-guide.md name the new flag on both commands; checked by --help output in the test and the doc diff.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
data.title: Active-only scan scoping: fsck and compact-all default to non-archived tickets with --include-archived override
